question: Why is the credits line ₹3.2 lakh?
answer: CloudDesk wants credits paid only if we claim in writing within 10 days. Our 14 software contracts with that wording recovered 22% of credits owed; automatic credits, today's wording and the benchmark, recover 94% (11 contracts). CloudDesk earned ₹4.5 lakh in credits over the last 12 months, so ₹4.5 lakh × (94% − 22%) = ₹3.2 lakh a year. Confidence is medium (14 contracts). Pooled data agrees: about 8 in 10 credits go unclaimed across 31 companies.

question: What if we accept a 15-day claim window?
answer: A 15-day claim would cost about ₹2.4 lakh a year, down from ₹3.2 lakh for 10 days. We have 0 own contracts with an 11–30 day window, so this uses pooled data: about 6 in 10 credits go unclaimed across 27 companies (40% recovered vs 94% automatic). Confidence is low. Package C's auto-filed 30-day claim is cheaper.

question: Show packages without the 3-year term
answer: Without the 3-year term, two packages remain. B “Pay faster” protects ₹10.5 lakh a year for paying in 30 days (about ₹22,000 a year), net ₹10.3 lakh, lead approval only. C “Meet halfway” protects ₹6.9 lakh with no cash give, lead approval only. Figures rest on 12 renewal, 14 credits and 9 price contracts.

question: Why is the renewal line ₹4.5 lakh?
answer: CloudDesk wants 90 days' notice instead of 30. In our history, 5 of 12 renewals with 60–90 days' notice went through without review, and unreviewed renewals left 18% of seats unused. 5/12 × 18% × ₹60 lakh = ₹4.5 lakh a year vs the opt-in benchmark. Today's 30-day notice already carries ₹1.1 lakh, so accepting adds ₹3.4 lakh a year. Confidence is medium (12 own contracts).

question: Why is the price line ₹3.8 lakh?
answer: CloudDesk wants to revise fees once a year with no cap. Our 9 software contracts with that wording rose 11.0% in year two; 10 contracts with a 5% cap rose 4.6%. (11.0% − 4.6%) × ₹60 lakh = ₹3.8 lakh a year vs the 5% cap benchmark. Your current fixed price is ₹2.8 lakh better than that benchmark, so accepting costs ₹6.6 lakh a year vs today. Confidence is medium (9 own contracts).
